title: The Beginning
description: The first years of F1 World Championship
highlights: The first F1 World Championship started at Silverstone in 1950
Alfa Romeo, Ferrari and Mercedes dominance
Drivers' courage and skill were at the forefront
technology: Front-engined, frame chassis cars. Engines in the 1.5-2.5 liter range, naturally aspirated. Tires were narrow and high-profile.
iconicMoments: 1950 Silverstone Grand Prix - The first race in F1 history
1951 German Grand Prix - Fangio's legendary Nürburgring victory
1955 Le Mans disaster - Mercedes' withdrawal from F1
1957 German Grand Prix - Fangio's last championship and legendary performance

keyDrivers.name: Alberto Ascari
keyDrivers.achievements: 2 World Championships, legendary period with Ferrari

safety: Safety measures were minimal. Drivers used helmets and leather suits. There were no safety barriers.
interestingFacts: Only 21 drivers in the first race
Fangio won championships with 4 different teams
Races in the 1950s usually lasted more than 3 hours
Drivers could also be car owners and mechanics

title: Golden Age
highlights: Lotus innovations under Colin Chapman's leadership
Golden age of classic tracks like Monaco, Monza and Silverstone
technology: Spread of rear-engined design. Engines 1.5-3.0 liter. Increasing use of fiberglass and aluminum.
iconicMoments: 1968 Lotus 49 - First sponsored car (Gold Leaf)
1963 Belgian Grand Prix - Race won by Jim Clark with a 4.5 minute lead
1965 Italian Grand Prix - Graham Hill's legendary Monza victory
1969 Monaco Grand Prix - Graham Hill's 5th Monaco victory

keyDrivers.name: Jim Clark
keyDrivers.achievements: 2 World Championships, won 25 races, Lotus legend

safety: Safety measures began to develop. Jackie Stewart became a pioneer of safety reforms. Safety barriers and helmet standards were improved.
interestingFacts: First sponsored car in 1968 (Lotus-Gold Leaf)
Jim Clark won 7 races in 1963
Graham Hill earned the title "King of Monaco"
Colin Chapman's "Add lightness" philosophy changed F1

title: Wings & Ground Effect
highlights: Niki Lauda's Nürburgring crash and return
James Hunt vs Niki Lauda rivalry
technology: Increased downforce with Ground Effect. Venturi tunnels and side pods. 3.0 liter naturally aspirated V8 engines.
iconicMoments: 1976 Japanese Grand Prix - Lauda's withdrawal from rainy race and Hunt's championship
1976 German Grand Prix - Niki Lauda's terrible crash at Nürburgring
1978 Italian Grand Prix - Mario Andretti's championship with Lotus
1979 French Grand Prix - Legendary passing battle between Arnoux and Villeneuve

keyDrivers.name: Niki Lauda
keyDrivers.achievements: 3 World Championships, return after Nürburgring crash

keyDrivers.name: James Hunt
keyDrivers.achievements: 1 World Championship, legendary rivalry with Lauda

safety: Safety measures were significantly improved. After the Nürburgring crash, safety standards were reviewed. Driver safety equipment was developed.
interestingFacts: Lotus 79 revolutionized with Ground Effect
Niki Lauda returned to racing 6 weeks after the crash
1976 season was one of the most dramatic seasons in F1 history
Ground Effect cars were very fast but dangerous

title: Turbo Era
highlights: Ayrton Senna vs Alain Prost legendary rivalry
technology: 1.5 liter turbo V6 engines, 1000+ HP power. Active suspension systems. Carbon fiber chassis becoming widespread.
iconicMoments: 1988 McLaren MP4/4 - Won 15 out of 16 races with Senna and Prost
1989 Japanese Grand Prix - Collision between Senna and Prost and championship
1986 Australian Grand Prix - Mansell's tire blowout and losing the championship
1982 Monaco Grand Prix - Riccardo Patrese's first victory and legendary finish

keyDrivers.name: Ayrton Senna
keyDrivers.achievements: 3 World Championships, won 41 races, legendary driver

safety: Safety measures were continuously improved. Carbon fiber chassis increased safety. Driver safety cell was developed.
interestingFacts: Turbo engines could produce 1000+ HP in qualifying
Rivalry between Senna and Prost is the most famous in F1 history
1988 McLaren MP4/4 is one of the most successful F1 cars
Turbo engines were banned in 1989

title: Electronic Revolution
highlights: ABS, Traction Control, Launch Control systems
technology: 3.5 liter naturally aspirated V10 engines. Traction Control, ABS, Launch Control. Carbon fiber monocoque chassis standard.
iconicMoments: 1994 San Marino Grand Prix - Senna's death and safety revolution
1993 European Grand Prix - Senna's legendary performance in the rain
1998 Belgian Grand Prix - Collision between Schumacher and Coulthard
1999 British Grand Prix - Schumacher finishing the race with a broken leg
safety: After the tragic crashes in 1994, a safety revolution began. Chicanes, safety barriers and driver safety equipment were improved. FIA tightened safety standards.
interestingFacts: Electronic aids were banned in 1994
Senna's death started the safety revolution in F1
Schumacher's F1 career began in this period
Williams FW14B and FW15C were the most advanced cars

title: Schumacher Era
technology: 3.0 liter V10 (2000-2005), 2.4 liter V8 (2006-2009). KERS system introduced. Aerodynamic complexity increased.

iconicMoments.text: 2000 Belgian Grand Prix - Hakkinen and Schumacher talk it out
Alonso became the youngest champion in 2005
2003 Brazilian Grand Prix - Fisichella Wins Amid Interlagos Chaos
2000 Japanese Grand Prix - Michael Schumacher Wins First Title With Ferrari

keyDrivers.name: Michael Schumacher
keyDrivers.achievements: 5 consecutive championships (2000-2004), legendary period with Ferrari

keyDrivers.name: Lewis Hamilton
keyDrivers.achievements: 1 World Championship (2008), first season with McLaren

safety: Safety standards were continuously improved. HANS device became mandatory. Track safety was increased.
interestingFacts: Schumacher won 13 races in 2004
Alonso became the youngest champion in 2005
Hamilton came very close to championship in his first season
KERS system was introduced in 2009

title: Hybrid Era
highlights: Transition to V6 Turbo Hybrid engines (2014)
Mercedes dominance in the hybrid era
technology: 1.6 liter V6 Turbo Hybrid engines. ERS (Energy Recovery System). DRS system. Halo safety system.

iconicMoments.text: 2018 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix - Three World Champions perform donuts
2016 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix - Rosberg's championship and retirement
2012 Brazilian Grand Prix - Vettel winning the championship on the last lap
2013 Indian Grand Prix – Vettel bows down to the RB9

keyDrivers.name: Max Verstappen
keyDrivers.achievements: Entry into F1, first race wins with Red Bull

safety: Halo safety system became mandatory in 2018. Safety standards reached the highest level.
engineSpecs: 1.6 liter V6 Turbo Hybrid, 850-1000 HP (including ERS)
interestingFacts: Mercedes established dominance in the hybrid era
Vettel won 4 consecutive championships with Red Bull
DRS system made overtaking easier
Halo system protected drivers

title: New Generation
highlights: New technical rules in 2022 and return of Ground Effect
Max Verstappen's dominance with Red Bull
technology: Ground Effect aerodynamics returned. 18-inch tires. Sustainable fuels. Budget cap.

iconicMoments.text: 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix - Verstappen's first championship
2021 Silverstone - Collision between Hamilton and Verstappen
2022 Brazilian Grand Prix - Legendary battle between Verstappen and Hamilton
2023 Monaco Grand Prix - Verstappen's legendary pole position in the rain

keyDrivers.name: Max Verstappen
keyDrivers.achievements: 3 World Championships (2021-2023), dominance with Red Bull

safety: Safety standards at the highest level. Halo system standard. Safety research continues.
engineSpecs: 1.6 liter V6 Turbo Hybrid, 1000+ HP (including ERS)
interestingFacts: 2021 season was one of the most dramatic seasons in F1 history
Rivalry between Verstappen and Hamilton
Ground Effect returned in 2022
Budget cap increased competition between teams
